message.content:
**Audit of bottom-sheet article reader (390px viewport)** 1) **Sheet layout** — Good. Grab handle is present and centered at the top of the sheet. Title "Chemotherapy: five things patients get wrong" wraps cleanly to 2 lines, bold and legible. Meta line renders exactly as "Dr. QA ProdOnco · Blog · 1 min read" with proper separators and muted styling. Body text is comfortable paragraph text with generous line-height and clear paragraph spacing. 2) **HTML conversion** — Clean. No raw `

`/`

` tags, no `&` or ` ` residue, no stray em-dash/quote encoding artifacts. Numbered items ("1. 'It is always painful'", "2. 'I will lose all my hair immediately'") render as plain text headings — acceptable, though they read slightly flat (could be styled as sub-headings for hierarchy). 3) **Close affordance** — Adequate but not explicit. Only a grab handle + implied swipe-down/scrim-tap; there's no visible ✕ button. The handle is a recognized iOS pattern, but an explicit close icon would help discoverability for less tech-savvy users (relevant for a healthcare audience). 4) **Overlap/cut-off** — No overlaps or misalignment inside the sheet. Text at the very bottom edge is naturally clipped mid-paragraph ("...whether your specific drugs are likely to cause"), which is fine since the content scrolls. Scrim correctly dims the doctor profile behind; sheet corner radius and elevation look consistent. 5) **Tone** — Calm, reassuring, and professional ("Pain is not the default experience", "temporary", "your oncologist can tell you upfront"). Appropriate for patient-facing oncology content; no alarmist language. **VERDICT: PASS** — clean layout, correct text conversion, and calm tone; only nitpick is the absence of an explicit close (✕) button, which is polish rather than a defect.

Handle present, title 2 lines, meta line correct, clean paragraphs, no HTML residue, numbered headings "1." etc. Close affordance: only grab handle, no X button — but swipe/handle may suffice; note scrim tap. Bottom text cut off is normal scroll. Minor: no explicit close button. Verdict PASS with note.
